news.title: Leandro Paredes handed massive punishment for World Cup Final brawl
news.lede: Leandro Paredes has received a lengthy ban for his role in the post-FIFA World Cup Final 2026 brawl. After Argentina fell short against Spain at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, USA, the defender engaged in a heated scuffle with members of the opposing team. While the World Cup final is designed to create action on the field, it was the drama that unfolded after the match that provided the biggest fireworks display of the evening. In a moment of madness, a furious Leandro Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat before launching Gavi towards the ground.

news.title: Leandro Paredes receives 10-match ban as Argentina punished for World Cup final brawl
news.lede: Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and Gavi also suspended. Fifa issue $321,000 fine for Falkland Islands banner. Three Argentina players have been banned for their part in a brawl at the end of last month’s World Cup final against Spain, but they have only been fined for displaying a Falkland Islands banner after the semi-final win over England. Leandro Paredes has been given a 10-match ban and a $90,000 (£66,000) fine by Fifa’s disciplinary committee, while Nahuel Molina was given a seven-match suspension and fined the same amount.

news.title: World Cup coming home? England prepares potential bid to host 2038 or 2042
news.lede: The long wait for a home tournamentAccording to The Sun , Great Britain is considering a bid to host either the 2038 or 2042 World Cup. Supported by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the proposal aims to bring football's flagship tournament back to British soil for the first time since 1966. With Burnham reportedly viewing a World Cup bid as a key driver for national investment, tourism, and urban regeneration, the tournament could finally return to British shores. Beyond its global tourist appeal and well-established transport network, Britain already possesses the world-class stadium infrastructure needed to host a tournament of this scale.The UK has not hosted the men's World Cup since 1966, although England hosted Euro 1996 and Wembley Stadium staged the Euro 2020 final.

news.title: FIFA World Cup final brawl: Leandro Paredes suspended for 10 matches, Argentina fined $321,000
news.lede: Argentine football player Leandro Paredes has been slapped with a 10-match suspension for being involved in a brawl after his team lost to Spain in the World Cup final received a 10-match suspension for his part in a brawl after his team lost to Spain in the World Cup final last month. His teammate Nahuel Molina has also been suspended for seven games, FIFA announced on Friday. A scuffle erupted following the final whistle when Argentina midfielder Paredes pushed Spain's Gavi to the ground as the European champions' substitutes rushed onto the field to celebrate. Paredes was charged on three assault counts, while Molina faced two.
